title: CISSP (2024 outline) practice exam
note: Original questions written for MyNextCert from ISC2's public CISSP exam outline (effective Apr 15, 2024). Not real exam questions. The real CISSP is adaptive (100-150 items in 3 hours, multiple choice and advanced item types); this is a fixed 125-item stand-in with 4 advanced items.

q.q: Your employer's code of conduct conflicts with the ISC2 Code of Ethics on a matter of public safety. Which should guide your action?
o: Right. The first ISC2 canon puts society and the common good ahead of other duties.
Duty to principals is the third canon, below society and honesty.
Age of a rule doesn't decide which duty comes first.
A manager's opinion can't override the canons.

q.q: Which list puts the four ISC2 Code of Ethics canons in the correct priority order, highest first?
o: Society; honor and law; principals; the profession
Right. Protect society, act honorably and legally, serve principals, then advance the profession.
Principals; society; the profession; honor and law
The profession; principals; society; honor and law
Honor and law; the profession; society; principals

q.q: A digitally signed email proves the sender can't later deny sending it. Which concept is this?
o: Right. A signature tied to the sender's private key prevents credible denial.
A signature alone doesn't hide the message.
Availability is about access when needed.
Accountability is related, but proof against denial is non-repudiation.

q.q: An attacker changes the destination account on a wire transfer while it's in transit. Which property was violated FIRST?
o: Right. The data was changed without authorization.
Reading wasn't the attack. Changing was.
The user was real. The data was altered.

q.q: Who is ULTIMATELY responsible for the security of an organization's information?
o: Right. Leadership is accountable, even when tasks are delegated.
Admins carry out controls, but accountability sits with leadership.
Custodians handle data day to day for the owner.
Auditors evaluate. They aren't accountable for security.

q.q: A company checks a vendor's security before signing, then keeps applying the agreed controls every day after. What do these two activities show, in order?
o: Right. Diligence is the research before acting; care is doing the right things ongoing.
Neither step avoids or accepts risk.
Separation of duties, then least privilege

q.q: Why should the security function report outside the IT department?
o: To avoid a conflict of interest
Right. Independence lets security challenge IT decisions.
Because IT never handles any security tasks at all
To lower the cost of the security team
So security can approve its own budget
No group should approve its own budget.

q.q: A U.S. company wants to ship strong encryption software to customers abroad. Which legal area must it check FIRST?
o: Right. Rules like the EAR can restrict exporting encryption technology.
Copyright protects expression, not export permission.

q.q: A company's secret recipe is protected only by confidentiality agreements and strict access controls. What type of intellectual property is this?
o: Right. Trade secrets are protected by keeping them secret, not by registration.
Copyright protects creative works, not a recipe's secrecy.

q.q: Personal data of EU residents is sent to a processor in a country without an EU adequacy decision. What does GDPR require?
o: Right. Transfers need adequacy or appropriate safeguards.
Nothing, as long as the data is encrypted in transit
Encryption helps but isn't a legal transfer basis.
Approval from each data subject's employer

q.q: Which type of investigation requires proof "beyond a reasonable doubt"?
o: Right. Criminal cases have the highest standard of proof.
Civil cases use a preponderance of the evidence.
Administrative reviews follow internal policy standards.
Regulatory standards vary but are lower than criminal.

q.q: HR asks security to look into an employee who broke the acceptable use policy. Nothing illegal is suspected. What type of investigation is this?
o: Right. Internal policy violations are administrative matters.
No lawsuit between parties is involved.

q.q: Which document is high-level, mandatory and approved by senior management?
o: Right. Policies state management's intent and direction.

q.q: A document recommends, but doesn't require, using a password manager. What is it?
During a BIA, the team finds the payroll process can be down for at most 3 days before the damage is unacceptable. What value is this?
o: Right. MTD is the longest a process can be unavailable.
ARO is how often a threat happens per year.

q.q: Why must the BIA include outside dependencies like payment processors and utilities?
o: A supplier failure can stop a process
Right. External dependencies can stop internal processes.
Suppliers write the organization's BC plan for it
The organization writes its own plan.
The BIA only covers external companies
It covers internal processes and what they depend on.

q.q: Why should an employee be required to take a mandatory vacation of two consecutive weeks?
o: Right. Fraud often surfaces when the person can't cover it up.
It reduces the company's payroll costs for the year
It replaces the need for job rotation
It's needed to renew their badge

q.q: An administrator is being fired. When should his access be removed?
o: At the time he's notified, or just before
Right. Removing access at notification prevents sabotage.
At the end of his last day
That leaves a window for damage.
After HR finishes the paperwork next week
Days of access is a big risk.

q.q: An asset is worth $200,000. A fire would destroy 40% of it, and fires happen once every 20 years. What is the ALE?
o: That's the SLE before applying the yearly rate.
That divides the asset value by 20 and skips the exposure factor.

q.q: A safeguard costs $6,000 per year and lowers ALE from $20,000 to $8,000. What is its yearly value to the company?
o: That's the ALE reduction before subtracting the safeguard's cost.
That subtracts the cost from the original ALE only.
That subtracts the cost from the new ALE.

q.q: Which risk analysis approach ranks risks using categories like High, Medium and Low instead of dollar values?
o: Right. Qualitative analysis uses relative ratings and judgment.
Quantitative uses numbers like SLE and ALE.

q.q: In STRIDE, an attacker uses a stolen session token to act as another user. Which threat category is this?
o: Right. Pretending to be someone else is spoofing identity.

q.q: Which threat modeling method is risk-centric and has seven stages, from defining objectives to analyzing risk and impact?
o: Right. PASTA is a seven-stage, risk-focused process.
STRIDE is a list of threat categories.

q.q: A company receives network switches from an unknown reseller at an unusually low price. Which supply chain risk is MOST likely?
o: Right. Gray-market gear may be fake or modified.
Too much rack space being used

q.q: Which artifact helps a company find out quickly whether vulnerable open-source components are in the software it buys?
o: Right. An SBOM lists the components inside the software.

q.q: How can a security team BEST measure whether its awareness program is working?
o: Track phishing click and report rates
Right. Behavior trends show whether training changes what people do.
Count how many slides are in each training deck
Ask employees if they liked the training
Record how long the training video is

q.q: New deepfake voice scams are targeting finance staff. How should the awareness program respond?
o: Add current examples and call-back checks
Right. Content must stay current with new attack methods.
Wait for next year's annual training
Tell staff to trust any voice they recognize
Remove phone calls from the training entirely this year
Phone scams are exactly the issue.

q.q: Who should decide the classification level of a data set?
o: Right. Owners are accountable for the data and set its classification.
Custodians protect data as the owner directs.
The help desk doesn't own data.

q.q: What is the MAIN reason to classify data?
o: To protect it according to its value
Right. Classification lets controls fit the data instead of treating everything the same.
To make every file encrypted in exactly the same way
Classification exists so controls can differ.
To reduce the number of files stored
To decide which employees get raises

q.q: A Confidential report must be sent to a partner. Which handling rule would a policy MOST likely require?
o: Encrypt it in transit and label it
Right. Handling rules cover marking, storage and transmission for each level.
Print it and leave copies in the lobby for pickup
Post it on the company website
Rename the file to hide its contents

q.q: Why must backup tapes carry the same classification label as the data on them?
o: Right. Media inherits the classification of what it holds.
Tapes are always lower risk than spinning disks
Tapes can hold just as much sensitive data.

q.q: Which practice is MOST important before you can protect assets?
o: Right. You can't protect what you don't know you have.
Tools don't replace knowing your assets.
Letting users install any software they like

q.q: An employee leaves the company. What should happen to the laptop and data issued to her?
o: Recover them and update the inventory
Right. Assets must be returned and their records kept current.
Let her keep the laptop as a thank-you
That takes company data out the door.
Ignore it if the laptop is old
Wait to see if she returns it
Recovery should be part of offboarding.

q.q: Which role carries out day-to-day backups and access controls for data, as the owner directs?
o: Right. Custodians protect and maintain the data.
Owners make decisions. Custodians carry them out.
That's the person the data describes.
Controllers decide why and how personal data is processed.

q.q: After files are deleted, traces of the data can still be recovered from the disk. What is this called?
o: Right. Remanence is the leftover data after deletion.

q.q: Which method BEST destroys data on a failed solid-state drive that can't be wiped?
o: Right. When a drive can't be sanitized, destroy it.
Degaussing doesn't work on flash memory.
The data is still on the chips.
Formatting it in another computer first
A format may not remove data, and the drive has failed.

q.q: Why is keeping data longer than required a risk?
o: It can be breached or demanded in a lawsuit
Right. Extra data means extra exposure and discovery costs.
Old data can still be encrypted.
Laws always require deleting data after one year
Retention periods vary by law and data.
Storage systems slow down with old files

q.q: A server's operating system reaches end of support next month. What should the asset plan include?
o: Replace or upgrade it in time
Right. Unsupported systems stop getting security fixes.
Keep it, since it still boots
Turn off its logging to save disk space

q.q: Which data state is HARDEST to protect with encryption alone?
o: Right. Data is usually decrypted in memory while it's processed.
Data at rest on a disk
Disk and database encryption protect it.
Data in transit over a network
Tapes can be encrypted at rest.

q.q: A company adopts the NIST moderate baseline, then removes controls that don't apply and adjusts others. What is this?
o: Right. Baselines are adjusted to fit the system.

q.q: Which technology keeps restrictions, like no printing, attached to a document wherever it goes?
o: Right. DRM controls use of the content itself.
Firewalls control traffic, not document use.

q.q: A system is set up so that if its access check fails, it denies access rather than allowing it. Which principle is this?
o: Right. Failures should leave the system in a safe state.

q.q: Which approach builds privacy into a system from the start rather than adding it later?
o: Right. Privacy is part of the design, not an afterthought.
Hiding details isn't privacy by design.
That's a general saying, not a design principle.

q.q: Which design goal is described as "keep it simple" to reduce flaws?
o: Right. Simpler designs have fewer places for bugs to hide.
Open design means security doesn't depend on secrecy.
That means controls should be easy to use.

q.q: Which model is about CONFIDENTIALITY and uses "no read up, no write down"?
o: Right. It stops secrets from leaking to lower levels.
Biba is about integrity: no read down, no write up.
Clark-Wilson enforces integrity through well-formed transactions.

q.q: A consultant who has seen Bank A's data is blocked from seeing its competitor Bank B's data. Which model is this?
o: Right. It changes access based on what the user has already seen.
BLP uses clearance levels, not conflicts of interest.
Take-Grant models how rights are passed.

q.q: Which model enforces integrity by having users change data only through approved programs and by separating duties?
o: Right. It uses well-formed transactions and separation of duties.
Graham-Denning defines rules for creating and deleting subjects and objects.

q.q: A system processes classified data and needs strict, label-based access. Which control approach fits the requirement BEST?
o: Right. MAC enforces labels the users can't change.
Owners could share data at will.

q.q: How should controls be chosen for a new system?
o: Based on its requirements and risk
Right. Requirements and risk drive control selection.
Based on whatever the last project happened to use
Based on what the vendor recommends

q.q: Which hardware component securely stores keys and supports measured boot on a laptop?
o: Right. The TPM protects keys and records boot measurements.

q.q: Which OS feature stops one process from reading another process's memory?
o: Right. Isolation keeps each process in its own space.
They lock or dim the screen.

q.q: Why are industrial control systems (ICS) hard to patch?
o: Downtime can halt operations or safety
Right. Availability and safety come first in ICS, so patching needs careful planning.
Their vendors are legally banned from releasing any patches
They are never connected to any network
They are always brand new and don't need patches

q.q: A web app takes user input and builds a database query directly from it. Which vulnerability is MOST likely?
o: Right. Unsanitized input in queries lets attackers run their own SQL.
CSRF tricks a user's browser into sending requests.
That's a memory flaw in low-level code.
Clickjacking hides elements to trick clicks.

q.q: Which risk is specific to serverless functions?
o: Right. Each function needs only the permissions it uses.
Unpatched host operating systems the customer must update
The provider manages the host in serverless.
Running out of hard drive space
Storage isn't managed that way in serverless.

q.q: Two parties need to agree on a shared secret key over an untrusted network without sending the key. Which method fits?
o: Right. It lets both sides derive the same key.
AES needs a key already agreed.

q.q: In PKI, which component confirms identity before a certificate authority issues a certificate?
o: Right. The RA verifies requesters for the CA.

q.q: Why do organizations plan for post-quantum cryptography now?
o: Data stolen now could be decrypted later
Right. "Harvest now, decrypt later" makes long-lived secrets urgent.
Quantum computers already break AES-256 easily
Post-quantum algorithms are faster than all current ones
Laws already ban RSA in every country

q.q: An attacker measures how long a server takes to process different inputs to learn its secret key. Which attack is this?
o: Right. Timing differences leak information about the key.
That guesses passwords from a word list.

q.q: An attacker captures a user's NTLM password hash and uses it to log in without cracking it. What is this?
o: Right. The hash itself is used to authenticate.
That targets service ticket hashes for offline cracking.
That uses known plaintext to find a key.

q.q: Which attack looks for two different inputs that produce the same hash?
o: Right. Collision attacks exploit the birthday paradox.
A brute-force attack on a password
That tries every key or password.
That studies letter frequency in ciphertext.

q.q: A company uses landscaping, lighting and clear sightlines around its building to discourage intruders. What approach is this?
o: Right. CPTED uses design to deter crime naturally.

q.q: Where should a data center ideally be placed inside a building?
o: In the center, away from outer walls
Right. Interior placement limits exposure to break-ins, weather and accidents.
On the ground floor, right next to the main entrance
In the basement below the water line
On the roof for easy cooling
Roofs face weather and access risks.

q.q: Which fire suppression system is BEST for a data center because water stays out of the pipes until a fire is confirmed?
o: Right. Pre-action needs two triggers before water enters the pipes.
Wet pipes are always full of water.
Deluge floods a whole area at once.

q.q: A brief, total loss of power is called what?
o: Right. A fault is a momentary loss of power. A blackout is prolonged.
A brownout is a long period of low voltage.
A spike is a short burst of high voltage.
A sag is a short period of low voltage.

q.q: Which control BEST protects servers from a short power failure while generators start?
o: Right. A UPS bridges the gap until the generator takes over.
It protects against spikes, not outages.

q.q: In the information system lifecycle, when should security requirements be defined?
o: Right. Early requirements are cheapest to build in.
Only after the system goes live
Never, if the system is only used internally

q.q: A system is being retired. Which step protects its data?
o: Right. Disposal must remove data and keep records accurate.
Unplug it and store it in a locked closet

q.q: At which OSI layer does a router make forwarding decisions using IP addresses?
o: Right. Routing by IP address is a Network layer job.

q.q: Which protocol should replace SNMPv2c for managing network devices securely?
o: Right. SNMPv3 adds authentication and encryption.

q.q: A company separates its payment card systems from the rest of its network to limit PCI DSS scope. What is this?
o: Right. Segmentation isolates sensitive systems and shrinks the audit scope.

q.q: Which IPsec mode encrypts the entire original IP packet and adds a new header, as used between two gateways?
o: Right. Tunnel mode wraps the whole packet, which suits site-to-site VPNs.
Transport mode protects only the payload.

q.q: In software-defined networking, what is separated from the data plane?
o: Right. SDN moves decisions to a central controller.

q.q: Which wireless security option gives each user their own credentials through 802.1X?
o: Right. Enterprise mode authenticates each user, usually through RADIUS.
Personal mode uses a shared passphrase.
MAC addresses are easy to spoof.

q.q: Microsegmentation and a policy that every request must be verified, wherever it comes from, are core parts of which architecture?
o: Right. Zero trust removes implicit trust inside the network.
A DMZ is one zone, not the whole approach.

q.q: Which device checks a laptop's patch level and antivirus before letting it onto the network?
o: Right. NAC checks device health before granting access.

q.q: Which transmission medium is hardest to tap without being noticed?
o: Right. Fiber doesn't leak signals the way copper does.
UTP emits signals that can be picked up.
Radio signals can be captured from a distance.

q.q: A core switch failure would take down the whole office. What design change fixes this?
o: Right. Redundancy removes the single point of failure.
Add more VLANs to the same core switch

q.q: Which endpoint control detects suspicious behavior on a laptop and can isolate it from the network?
o: Right. EDR monitors, alerts and can isolate hosts.
KVM switches share keyboards and monitors.

q.q: Why should network device firmware be kept current?
o: Right. Unpatched network gear is a common way in.
Updates make cables carry more data
Updates are needed for warranty only
Updates remove the need for device passwords

q.q: Remote staff need encrypted access to internal apps from home. Which option fits BEST?
o: Right. The VPN encrypts traffic, and MFA protects the login.
Opening RDP directly to the internet
Exposed RDP is a top attack target.
Using plain FTP to move files

q.q: Which protocol protects voice-over-IP media streams?
o: Right. Secure RTP encrypts the voice and video media.

q.q: A partner connects to your network to exchange orders. What should govern that connection?
o: Right. Third-party links need documented, monitored security terms.
Trust, since the partner is a large and well-known company
An open firewall rule from any partner IP

q.q: Video meetings share confidential designs. Which control MOST directly protects them?
o: Right. Encryption and controlled access protect the content.
A larger screen in the room
Public meeting links posted on the company website

q.q: Which protocol and port should replace plain HTTP for a login page?
o: Right. TLS encrypts the login and session.

q.q: Which remote access approach gives contractors app access without putting their devices on the internal network?
o: Right. Only the screen reaches the contractor; data stays inside.
A full-tunnel VPN for every contractor laptop
That brings unmanaged devices onto the network.

q.q: Which control type is a badge reader on a server room door?
o: Right. It controls entry to a physical space.
Logical controls protect systems and data.
Corrective controls fix problems after they happen.

q.q: Why should access to a company's code repositories be controlled as tightly as access to its servers?
o: Code and its secrets are valuable
Right. Repos often hold secrets and logic attackers want.
Servers don't need access control at all

q.q: Which authentication factor type is a fingerprint?
A biometric system is tuned so it rarely lets in the wrong person but sometimes rejects the right one. Which error is being kept low?
o: Right. Lowering FAR makes it harder for impostors, often raising false rejections.
FRR is rising in this setup.
CER is where FAR and FRR are equal.
That's about users who can't register.

q.q: Why are session timeouts important after a user logs in?
o: They limit misuse of idle sessions
Right. Expiring sessions reduces hijacking risk.
They're only needed on public kiosks

q.q: In SAML federation, which party issues the assertion that a user has authenticated?
o: Right. The IdP authenticates the user and sends the assertion.
The user's browser on its own
The browser carries it, but the IdP issues it.
DNS isn't part of SAML authentication.

q.q: A company uses its on-premises directory to log users in to cloud SaaS apps. What is this setup called?
o: Right. On-premises identity is federated to cloud services.

q.q: Which access model grants access using attributes like department, device health and time of day?
o: Right. ABAC evaluates many attributes in its policies.

q.q: In an access control architecture, which component makes the allow or deny decision?
o: Right. The PDP evaluates policy and decides.

q.q: A login system asks for extra verification when a user signs in from a new country. Which approach is this?
o: Right. The system adjusts requirements based on risk signals.
Location and risk drive this, not time.

q.q: During an access review, a manager finds an analyst still has admin rights from a previous job. What is this?
o: Right. Access built up across job changes.

q.q: Which account type needs special handling because no person logs in with it, yet it often has broad access?
o: Right. They need owners, least privilege and credential rotation.

q.q: An attacker uses a flaw to go from a normal user account to administrator. What is this called?
o: Right. It's gaining higher rights than granted.

q.q: In Kerberos, what does the Key Distribution Center issue first after the user authenticates?
o: Right. The TGT is then used to request service tickets.

q.q: Why must clocks be synchronized in a Kerberos environment?
o: Right. Time checks help stop replay attacks.
Kerberos encrypts all data with the current time
Clocks decide which users are admins

q.q: Which protocol adds an identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 for user login?
o: Right. OIDC adds ID tokens for authentication.
Kerberos is a separate ticket system.

q.q: Users store dozens of passwords. Which tool reduces reuse while keeping them protected?
o: Right. Vaults generate unique passwords and store them encrypted.
Writing them on a desk calendar

q.q: A file owner shares a folder with two coworkers by choice. Which access model is this?
o: Right. Owners decide who gets access.
MAC uses labels set by the system.

q.q: Why use an independent third party for some security assessments?
o: Right. Independence increases trust in the results.
Because internal teams aren't allowed to run tests
Internal testing is common and useful.
Because third parties never miss anything

q.q: Before a penetration test begins, what must be agreed in writing?
o: Right. Written permission and scope make the test legal and safe.
Nothing, if the tester is experienced and certified

q.q: A company tests both its main data center and its remote branch offices. Which strategy element does this cover?
o: Right. Strategies should cover every site, not just headquarters.
That's a control, not a strategy element.

q.q: Which team defends during an exercise while the red team attacks?
o: Right. Blue teams detect and respond.
Purple teams combine red and blue to improve together.
That isn't a standard exercise role.

q.q: Testers are given full knowledge of the system, including source code and network diagrams. What kind of test is this?
o: Black-box testers get no inside information.
Blind testing means the testers start with no information.

q.q: Which test feeds random, malformed input to a program to find crashes?
o: That reads code without running it.
That checks old features still work.

q.q: A team runs a safe, automated simulation of real attack techniques to check whether detections fire. What is this?
o: Right. It continuously tests whether controls detect known techniques.

q.q: Which is a KEY RISK INDICATOR rather than a performance indicator?
o: Number of training sessions held this quarter
Help desk tickets closed per day

q.q: Why should backup verification data be collected regularly?
o: To prove backups can actually be restored
Right. Verification data shows recovery will work.
Because backups expire legally after a month

q.q: A vulnerability can't be fixed for 90 days because of a vendor dependency. What should happen?
o: Right. Exceptions must be formal, time-limited and approved.
Ignore it until the vendor eventually fixes it

q.q: A researcher finds a flaw in a vendor's product. What is the responsible way to report it?
o: Right. Coordinated disclosure protects users while the fix is made.
That helps attackers before a fix exists.
Sell it to the highest bidder on a forum

q.q: Who should receive an executive summary of a penetration test?
o: Right. Leaders need impact and priorities, not raw tool output.

q.q: A customer audits a vendor's controls under the right-to-audit clause in their contract. Which kind of audit is this?
o: Right. An outside party audits another organization.
Internal audits are done by the organization's own auditors.

q.q: Which SOC report is meant for public distribution?
o: Right. SOC 3 is a general-use summary.
SOC 1 is for financial reporting auditors.

q.q: Why should audit findings be tracked to closure?
o: Right. Findings without follow-up leave the risk in place.
So the audit can be skipped entirely next year
To find out who to blame
Tracking is about fixing, not blaming.

q.q: Why review logs as part of security control testing?
o: To confirm controls log what they should
Right. Logs show whether detective controls actually work.
To delete old entries and save space
Because logs replace penetration tests completely

q.q: Which data shows whether account management is working?
o: Right. Leftover accounts show gaps in deprovisioning.
The color of the login page
The number of printers on each floor

q.q: Which evidence should be collected FIRST from a live system?
o: Right. Collect in order of volatility, most volatile first.

q.q: What does chain of custody prove about evidence?
o: Who handled it, and that it's unaltered
Right. It shows the evidence is trustworthy in court.
That the investigation is finished and closed

q.q: Which monitoring focuses on data leaving the organization's network?
o: Right. It watches outbound traffic for exfiltration.
That copies traffic but isn't a monitoring focus.

q.q: A tool learns each user's normal behavior and alerts when an account suddenly downloads far more than usual. What is it?
o: Right. UEBA flags deviations from normal behavior.

q.q: Servers are built automatically from scripts that apply the approved baseline every time. Which benefit does this give MOST?
o: Right. Automation prevents drift and human error.
It removes the need for patching
It makes servers immune to attacks
It removes the need for change control entirely
Changes to the scripts still need control.

q.q: A server's settings no longer match the approved baseline, with no record of why. What is this?
o: Right. Unrecorded changes moved it away from the baseline.

q.q: Moving staff through different roles periodically helps detect fraud and spreads knowledge. What is this?
o: Right. Rotation reveals irregularities and builds backup skills.
That requires two people for one task.

q.q: Opening the company vault requires two people, each with half the combination. What principle is this?
o: Right. No one person can act alone.
Related, but this is specifically dual control.

q.q: How should backup tapes be moved to an offsite vault?
o: Encrypted and tracked by a bonded courier
Right. Media in transit needs protection and accountability.
In an employee's personal car, with no records kept
Left at the front desk for pickup

q.q: Which practice protects data on laptops if they're lost?
o: Right. Encrypted disks are unreadable without the key.

q.q: After an incident is contained and systems are restored, what should the team do next?
o: Right. The review improves the process for next time.
Blame the user who clicked the link
Reviews focus on process, not blame.

q.q: In ISC2's incident management steps, which step comes right after detection?
o: Right. Detection, response, mitigation, reporting, recovery, remediation, lessons learned.
Mitigation (containing the damage) comes after response starts.
Recovery comes after mitigation and reporting.

q.q: A decoy server is set up to attract attackers and study their methods. What is it?
o: Right. Honeypots lure attackers away from real systems.
A bastion host is a hardened, exposed server.
A jump box is an admin access server.

q.q: Suspicious email attachments are opened in an isolated environment to see what they do. What is this?
o: Right. A sandbox runs untrusted content safely.

q.q: A critical patch is released for an internet-facing server. What is the BEST order?
o: Test, deploy via change control, verify
Right. Test, deploy and verify, quickly for critical exposed systems.
Deploy to production first, then test
Wait six months to see if others have problems
That leaves a critical gap open.
Skip it because the server still works
Working isn't the same as secure.

q.q: How should vulnerability fixes be prioritized?
o: Easy isn't the same as important.
By the date the scanner was first installed

q.q: What should happen BEFORE a change is approved?
o: Impact analysis and a back-out plan
Right. Approval depends on understanding risk and having a rollback.
It's deployed to production first to test it
The change board is skipped for speed

q.q: An admin makes an emergency firewall change to stop an attack. What must happen afterward?
o: Document it and review it afterward
Right. Emergency changes still go through review.
Nothing, since it was an emergency
Undo it immediately once the attack stops
Undoing may reopen the hole; review first.
Delete the logs of the change

q.q: Which recovery site has equipment and current data ready, so it can take over within hours or less?
o: Right. Hot sites are fully ready.
Cold sites have space and power only.
Warm sites need time to be readied.
Mobile sites must be delivered and set up.

q.q: Which RAID level mirrors data on two disks?
o: Right. RAID 1 writes the same data to both disks.
RAID 10 needs at least four disks.

q.q: During a disaster, who should communicate with the public about the outage?
o: The spokesperson named in the plan
Right. One trained voice keeps messages accurate.
That leads to mixed and wrong messages.
The attacker, if it's a cyberattack

q.q: What is the FIRST priority in any disaster recovery effort?
o: Right. Life safety always comes first.

q.q: The recovery site runs real workloads at the same time as production, without stopping the primary site. Which test is this?
o: Right. Both sites run; production isn't interrupted.
That shuts down the primary site.

q.q: Which DR test is MOST realistic but also MOST risky?
o: Right. Production really fails over, so a problem causes a real outage.

q.q: Who should approve the business continuity plan?
o: Right. Leadership owns the business and its continuity.
The vendor that sold the backup software
Vendors don't own your BC plan.

q.q: Why exercise the BC plan regularly?
o: Changes can make the plan unworkable
Right. Exercises keep the plan current and the team ready.
Plans legally expire every month unless renewed
Staff must be able to use them.

q.q: Which perimeter control BEST stops vehicles from ramming a building entrance?
o: Right. Bollards block vehicles while letting people through.
Lights deter, but don't stop vehicles.

q.q: Which control detects someone in a server room after hours?
o: Right. They detect presence and raise an alert.
Locks prevent entry but don't detect.
A fire extinguisher by the door

q.q: An employee is forced at gunpoint to open a secure door. What should a good duress system let them do?
o: Send a silent alarm while complying
Right. Duress codes signal for help without alerting the attacker.
Sound a loud siren immediately to scare them
That could put the employee in danger.

q.q: Before an employee travels to a high-risk country, which precaution helps protect company data?
o: Right. Loaners limit what's exposed if the device is seized or tampered with.
Share the admin password with the hotel's IT staff

q.q: Which maturity model measures how well an organization builds security into software?
o: Right. SAMM assesses software assurance maturity.

q.q: In DevSecOps, when are security checks run?
o: Right. Security is built into every stage.
Never, to keep release speed high

q.q: Why should software changes go through change management even in Agile teams?
o: So changes are reviewed and traceable
Right. Agile speeds delivery but still needs control over production.
Agile teams are banned from releasing code to production

q.q: Developers keep committing API keys to the code repository. Which control helps MOST?
o: Secret scanning plus a secrets vault
Right. Scanning blocks leaks, and a vault removes the need to hard-code.
Making the repository public for transparency
Shorter keys are weaker and still leak.
Leaked secrets must be rotated anyway.

q.q: Why should third-party libraries be scanned during the build?
o: Right. Software composition analysis finds vulnerable components.
They make the code run slower
They're always written in a different language

q.q: Which test analyzes a running web app from the outside for flaws like XSS?
o: Right. DAST attacks the running app.
Unit tests check small pieces of logic.

q.q: Why should changes to production code be logged and audited?
o: Right. Audit trails support accountability and investigations.
Because logs replace code reviews for every change

q.q: After a release, a risk analysis finds a new feature exposes sensitive data. What should happen?
o: Track it as a risk to fix
Right. Findings feed back into development.
Ignore it until a customer complains about it
Mark the feature as secure anyway

q.q: Before buying a SaaS product, what should the security team review?
o: Its security reports and contract terms
Right. Acquired services must meet your requirements.
Nothing, since SaaS security is entirely the provider's problem
The customer keeps accountability for its data.

q.q: A team wants to use an open-source library maintained by one volunteer with no updates for three years. What is the MAIN risk?
o: Right. Abandoned components don't get security patches.
The license will cost too much
Open source is usually free to use.
It's illegal to use open source in business

q.q: Which assurance helps when buying commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software?
o: Right. Evidence of testing and support shows how risky it is.
The number of colors in the UI
How popular the vendor is on social media sites

q.q: Which coding practice BEST prevents cross-site scripting (XSS)?
o: Right. Output encoding keeps input from running as script.
Storing passwords in plain text in the database

q.q: An API returns other customers' records when a user changes the ID in the URL. What flaw is this?
o: Broken object-level authorization (insecure direct object reference)
Right. The API doesn't check that the user owns the record.
CSRF abuses a logged-in user's browser.

q.q: Why should error messages shown to users avoid stack traces and SQL details?
o: Right. Generic errors avoid information leaks.
They break the website's colors and layout

q.title: Pick the risk response
q.scenario: Five risks after an assessment. Pick the response that fits each one best.

rows.req: A low-value internal wiki has a minor flaw that would cost more to fix than any likely loss.
rows.why: Low risk and high fix cost suit documented acceptance.

rows.req: A planned feature would store card numbers it doesn't need. The team drops the feature.
rows.why: Removing the risky activity avoids the risk.

rows.req: Admin logins have no MFA. The team adds MFA.
rows.why: Adding a control reduces the risk.

rows.req: The company buys cyber insurance for breach costs.
rows.why: Insurance shifts financial impact to another party.

rows.req: A web server is unpatched. The team patches it.

q.title: Match the security model
q.scenario: Four rules. Pick the security model each one comes from. Two options are distractors.

items.text: A Secret user can't read Top Secret data or write to Unclassified.
items.why: No read up, no write down protects confidentiality.

items.text: A user can't read lower-integrity data or write to higher-integrity data.
items.why: No read down, no write up protects integrity.

items.text: Users change data only through approved programs, with duties split.
items.why: Well-formed transactions and separation of duties.

items.text: Seeing one client's data blocks access to a competitor's data.
items.why: The Chinese Wall model prevents conflicts of interest.

q.title: Pick the access control model
q.scenario: Five access rules. Pick the model each one uses.

rows.req: A file's owner decides who can read it.
The system enforces Secret and Top Secret labels that users can't change.
rows.why: Labels and clearances are mandatory access control.

rows.req: Everyone in the Nurse group gets the same chart access.
The firewall blocks all inbound traffic except HTTPS for everyone.
rows.why: One rule applies to all subjects.

rows.req: Access needs Finance department, a managed device and a U.S. location.

q.title: Match the DR test
q.scenario: Four DR test descriptions. Pick the test type each one describes. Two options are distractors.

items.text: Team members each review the plan on their own and send comments.
items.why: A read-through (checklist) review is individual and document-based.

items.text: The team meets and talks through a scenario step by step.
items.why: A walkthrough (tabletop) is a group discussion.

items.text: The recovery site processes real work while production keeps running.
items.why: A parallel test runs both without stopping production.

items.text: Production is shut down and operations move to the recovery site.
items.why: A full interruption test really fails over.

q.title: Pick the testing approach
q.scenario: Four testing needs. Pick the approach that fits each one best.

rows.req: Simulate an outside attacker who knows nothing about the network.
rows.why: Black-box testers start with no inside knowledge.

rows.req: Review every code path with full access to source and diagrams.
Test as a partner who has a normal user account but no diagrams.
Throw malformed input at a file parser to find crashes.

q.title: Name the data role
q.scenario: Four people and what they do with data. Pick the role each one holds.

rows.req: The VP of Sales decides how customer data is classified and who may see it.
rows.why: Owners are accountable and set classification.

rows.req: The database admin runs backups and applies the access rules the owner set.
Under GDPR, the company decides why and how customers' personal data is processed.
A payroll vendor processes employee data only on the company's instructions.
rows.why: Processors act on the controller's instructions.
